description: In an economy, the financial market is a mechanism that facilitates the flow of funds between savers and investors. Based on the maturity period of the financial instruments, it is broadly classified into the Money Market and the Capital Market.

sections.title: Introduction to Financial Market
sections.description: The basic classification of the two main components of the financial market and the fundamental differences between them.

key_concepts.explanation: The market for short-term funds where the maturity period of financial instruments is one year or less. It is primarily used by institutions for managing short-term liquidity.
The market for long-term funds where the maturity period of financial instruments is more than one year. It is primarily used for business expansion and capital formation.

important_facts.fact: In India, the Money Market is regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), whereas the Capital Market is regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).

sections.title: Instruments of Money Market
sections.description: Major financial instruments used by governments and corporations to raise short-term funds.

key_concepts.explanation: Short-term instruments issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on behalf of the Central Government. They are issued for maturities of 91 days, 182 days, and 364 days, and are considered the safest money market instrument with zero default risk.
Unsecured promissory notes issued by large, highly creditworthy corporate entities to raise short-term funds directly from the market.
Short-term, negotiable, and unsecured financial instruments issued by commercial banks and development financial institutions to raise bulk deposits.
Money borrowed or lent for just one day (overnight) strictly for interbank transactions. If the money is borrowed for a period of 2 to 14 days, it is known as 'Notice Money'.

sections.title: Structure of Capital Market
sections.description: Classification of the capital market based on the issuance and trading of long-term securities.

key_concepts.explanation: Also known as the New Issue Market (NIM), it is the market where new securities are issued for the very first time. The most common method of raising capital here is through an Initial Public Offering (IPO).
Commonly known as the Stock Exchange, it is the market where already issued (existing) securities are traded among investors. It provides liquidity and marketability to existing assets.
The market exclusively dealing with government and semi-government securities. 'Gilt-edged' implies the best quality, indicating that these securities carry zero default risk.

sections.title: Stock Exchanges and Key Terminology
sections.description: India's prominent stock exchanges and crucial terms associated with stock market trading.

key_associations.extra_info: It is the benchmark sensitivity index of the BSE, designed to measure the overall performance of the top 30 largest and most actively traded stocks.
It is the benchmark index of the NSE, comprising the 50 top companies representing 13 different sectors of the Indian economy.
A 'Bull' is a speculator who expects a rise in stock prices, whereas a 'Bear' is a speculator who expects a fall in stock prices.

sections.title: Important Institutions and Historical Events
sections.description: Establishment years and significance of major institutions that shaped the Indian financial market.

historical_events.significance: It was established by the prominent businessman Premchand Roychand and holds the distinction of being Asia's oldest stock exchange.

historical_events.event: Establishment of NSE and Statutory Status to SEBI
historical_events.significance: NSE was established as India's first fully automated electronic trading exchange. In the same year, SEBI was granted statutory status through the SEBI Act, 1992.

important_facts.fact: A Demat Account stands for Dematerialized Account, which is mandatory for investors to hold shares and securities in an electronic (digital) format rather than as physical certificates.
